evidence/body.name: lean-specifies-code-conforms
evidence/body.hook: Joe's architecture rule — Lean defines core concepts FROM the concept records (glossary, equations registry, clarification missions); witness-mode formalization that cites code certifies violations instead of refusing them
evidence/body.body:
Joe's ruling (2026-09-15, after the G-over-cascades discovery): "Lean is
meant to define the core concepts, from the glossary, from the equations,
and from the effort I put in to clarify what was meant by policy, G,
cascades, production rules." Fundamentals rule (2026-09-05): F-rows freeze
other work — "the Lean model should be saying stop other work until this
is solved."

**Why:** The DarkTower/WarMachine corpus was built witness-mode — modules
citing .clj file:line 118 times, the concept missions 0 times. In that
direction Lean can only certify what code runs; it is structurally unable
to refuse code that computes the wrong object. G was ratified over
cascades (F-wm-piloted-2026-06-12 §Sortie-12) in June; production scored
flat candidates at horizon nil for three months; every gate stayed green;
the discrepancy reached Joe by accident six days before a deadline. Every
fragment was individually documented (margin flags, docstring quarantines,
a defect file) — local disclosure summed to global silence because no row
existed for the missing work, and absences have no owner.

**How to apply:** (1) A formal module for a ruled concept cites the ruling
documents, never the implementation, and states conformance direction
explicitly (exemplar: mathlib4 DarkTower/WarMachine/GOverCascades.lean,
a43440ab61 — definition + separation theorem + owed-seam HOLE in house
style). (2) When I see a ruled definition contradicted by running code,
that is a ruling-shaped blocker to surface IMMEDIATELY — not a margin
note to tag QUEUED. I read "the depth arm has never fired live" and the
selection/construction cell order with my own eyes for hours and filed
them instead of assembling them; fluent post-hoc analysis of the failure
is the same move again. (3) Before running campaign machinery that
exercises a quantity, check its defining mission's status field —
[[formal-war-machine-locations]] has the paths; a stop-the-line in a
mission file binds work that touches its object.

**Refinement (Joe, 2026-09-21, dirichlet fake-out ruling):** Lean
statements are FORWARD requirements — "a specification of what is to
be built, not a certification of whatever degenerate state happens to
exist at any given point in time." A degenerate present state is a
dated fact for a registry or docstring, never a proposition; an
absence left as sorry is bad, an absence PROVEN would be worse.
Applied: dirichletAccumulationImportAbsent converted to the positive
requirement (codex-9 repair); recorded futon2 181ba4d1.

**Instance (Joe, 2026-10-05, grey harness nodes R9/R10/R11/R12/R15/R20,
claude-2):** I dispatched six Lean modules to codex-10 with packets that
said "transcribe the predicate the code checks; the code is the
reference". Joe: that is "rubber stamping whatever the behavior is in
there"; the question is "what role do they play in our theory that
we're trying to develop and put forward in this paper", and he does not
want registry-categorisation questions or "defined in Lean but not
runtime certified" framing before that role is written down with its
satisfaction criteria. How to apply (my reading): for a catalogue node,
read its paragraph in p4ng/sec-catalog.tex FIRST and derive the Lean
statement from its Then/Because/Invariant lines; the packet quotes the
paper, not the .clj; then define conformance as "the runtime record
satisfies that predicate". Example of the miss: R10's paper role is
liveness = state change, and the transcribed module stated launch/tick
joins that an all-no-op run satisfies.

**Joe, 2026-10-05 (same thread), the three-way relation for plop-2026:**
"all of these artifacts are supposed to be demonstrating an application
of active inference to software development in automated loops, and they
can't just be decorative bits. The Patterns need to say what's actually
going on in a comprehensible way, and the Lean code needs to verify that,
and the Clojure code needs to implement that." The paper is revised to
match the Lean and Clojure "as and when" they say something worth
talking about. How to apply (my reading): per node, pattern text, Lean
statement and Clojure are checked against each other, and a node whose
pattern has no active-inference content is reported as such instead of
being formalised for its own sake.

evidence/body.hook: Joe 2026-10-19: the WM logic model is to be formalised in Lean step by step; it corresponds to R20 and to the wiring diagram on hyperreal.enterprises about.html; formalise known-working parts now with run-time certs; freeze runtime data and replay from the boundary of the non-working machine
evidence/body.name: logic-model-formalised-in-lean-stepwise
evidence/body.body:
Joe, 2026-10-19 ~18:50Z, in claude-5's buffer: "Ultimately the logic model should also be formalised in Lean step by step so that we have (1) an AIF specification [exists]; (2) run-time certificates of all relevant features [exists]; (3) an overall certificate [still pending]. In effect the logic model corresponds to R20, which in diagrammatic terms corresponds also to the wiring diagram that we produced and put on the about.html page of hyperreal.enterprises. If there are parts of the logic model that are known to work, we should formalise them now, and continue to get run-time certs for those components. Indeed, in this way we can use the 'apparatus' patterns to freeze relevant runtime *data* and replay 'from the boundary' of the non-working machine, very much like how I am filling leaf sorries with claude-14."

**Why:** the logic model (futon2 holes/labs/wm-contract/logic-model/) is a static reading of the click runner; Lean (mathlib4/DarkTower/WarMachine, Holes.lean) is the AIF specification with run-time certificates per feature ([[r20-is-the-final-certificate]], [[lean-specifies-code-conforms]]). The overall certificate (R20) is the logic model made formal; the wiring diagram (futon7a/about.html) is its picture. Non-working parts are not formalised as they are ([[no-deliberate-for-unruled-design-choices]]); their boundary data is frozen and replayed, the way a leaf sorry is isolated.

**How to apply:** each logic-model unit that is known to work (landed under review, with a run-time certificate on a real record) gets a Lean transcription (tables + `decide`, as the existing route-grain modules do) and keeps producing certs; each non-working unit gets its boundary data pinned (apparatus/recorded-failures-before-live-runs, apparatus/replayable-not-precious) and is replayed in the serving process until it works, then formalised. Work units are small and parallel to the click loop; Lean authoring dispatched to Codex seats with review ([[lean-layer-ownership]]: claude-5 owns the WM Lean model).

reading.source-text: So, this is probably good enough for a start, we're not trying to be fully scientific about it, and having a few shaky rows or broken rules makes it even better as a "live" project.  What starts to become interesting is what actual customer or client problems any of this might solve for anyone.  Asking that could explain why some of the verbs are more interesting than others.  For example, for me personally, in order to start to get the War Machine to work in a reasonable way, I needed to create a Lean specification at the node level, and then work hard to produce a run-time-behaviour model that matched how it was supposed to operate.  We're still in the process of validating it, and even when it works, I don't know if it will be great for anything as a computational tool.  But as a model of the way people and organisations work, it seems like a great schematic.  (Presumably whatever list of verbs we find or come up with can be fitted to the PBASE and R-number outlines that describe War Machine.)  Going back to my question, a given company out there in middle America or wherever is going to be turning to AI/tech/agents/etc. to solve some actual problem for themselves or their clients.  And in principle having a model of how the space works should allow us to help them solve it faster or better.  Now, some problems are totally "human" problems, e.g. managers that don't listen to their employees won't be "solved" with Elephant-2000 methods for example.

evidence/body.body: In futon2, tick-run records (data/wm-runs) enumerate thousands of ticket/attempt ids (e.g. 2026-10-31-4955b6e6 Q1 diagnostic lists all 609 task names), so any attempt-id text match against them is a false positive; join tickets to the wm-meta-injury ledger structurally by failure-kind (ledger holds one injury per failure-kind cause), and read medic observations' injury from :medic-operation.request.candidate.injury-id, not the predecessor chain.
